title: Tamil Nadu Politics – Evening Brief – 15 November 2026
headline: Political Tensions Mount in Tamil Nadu Over Alliance Rifts, Mekedhatu Dispute, and High-Profile Legal Battles

sections.big_picture:
Tamil Nadu's political landscape is witnessing intense friction as opposition leaders pressure Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay to challenge the Congress high command over Karnataka's Mekedhatu dam project ahead of his scheduled visit to New Delhi. Concurrently, intra-alliance strains have surfaced publicly, highlighted by sharp exchanges between Congress leaders and ruling party members regarding law and order and controversial legislator conduct. 

At the same time, state administration faces severe scrutiny over rising inflation and economic pressures, while anti-corruption agencies and federal investigative bodies pursue high-profile cases against political figures across party lines. These compounding legislative, fiscal, and diplomatic challenges underscore a volatile governance climate as parties realign for upcoming electoral milestones and state-level policy battles.

top_developments.headline: AIADMK and AMMK Press CM Vijay to Confront Congress High Command on Mekedhatu Dam Issue During Delhi Visit
top_developments.summary: AIADMK general secretary Edappadi K Palaniswami and AMMK general secretary T.T.V. Dhinakaran have publicly urged Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay to leverage his upcoming New Delhi visit to challenge the Congress leadership over Karnataka's proposed Mekedhatu dam project. Chief Minister Vijay is scheduled to travel to the national capital to attend the formal launch of Congress Parliamentary Party chairperson Sonia Gandhi's memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love, following a personal invitation. top_developments.headline: ED Re-Summons Former Minister C. Vijayabaskar and Wife in Rs 35.79 Crore Disproportionate Assets Case
top_developments.summary: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has issued fresh summons to former AIADMK minister C. Vijayabaskar, who recently aligned with the TVK, and his wife in connection with an ongoing money laundering probe linked to a Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption (DVAC) case. The federal investigation centers on allegations of amassing disproportionate assets valued at Rs 35.79 crore during his tenure as a state minister. Federal investigators are probing financial trails and real estate transactions allegedly connected to disproportionate wealth accumulation identified in the initial state anti-corruption filings. sections.government_and_administration: - **Higher Education Minister P. Viswanathan and TNCC Leaders Clash Over Alliance Dynamics and Law and Order:** Higher Education Minister P. Viswanathan publicly questioned former Tamil Nadu Congress Committee (TNCC) president K. Selvaperunthagai's political allegiance following sharp criticism from the Congress leader regarding the alliance government's handling of law and order. Speaking to reporters at the Chennai airport, Mr. Viswanathan dismissed Mr. Selvaperunthagai's remarks and demanded clarification on his future political trajectory before responding to governance queries. The public spat erupted against the backdrop of internal disagreements over a Kallakurichi TVK legislator accused of sexual misconduct, whom senior Congress figures had controversially defended. Minister Viswanathan defended the administration's six-month record in higher education, highlighting systemic reforms such as transparent principal appointments across 118 colleges without bribery. Opposition parties, meanwhile, have seized upon these intra-alliance fissures to question the stability and administrative competence of the ruling coalition. ([DT Next](https://www.dtnext.in/news/tamilnadu/minister-viswanathan-questions-selvaperunthagais-political-allegiance))
sections.political_parties_and_opposition: - **AMMK General Secretary T.T.V. Dhinakaran Slams State Government Over Retail Inflation Spike:** Amma Makkal Munnetra Kazhagam (AMMK) general secretary T.T.V. Dhinakaran censured the TVK-led government on Saturday, highlighting that Tamil Nadu currently ranks first in India for retail inflation, which has surged to 7.29 per cent. Addressing the media, Mr. Dhinakaran accused the administration of administrative negligence and failing to implement timely market interventions to control skyrocketing prices of essential commodities. He asserted that the current economic hardship faced by citizens stems directly from a lack of monitoring by state economic authorities. Concurrently, AIADMK leaders including former minister Sellur Raju echoed these grievances, criticizing the administration's welfare delivery and predicting that the current government would not complete its full five-year term due to internal contradictions. ([The Hindu](https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/tamil-nadu/take-necessary-steps-to-control-inflation-dhinakaran-tells-tn-govt/article71701530.ece))
sections.assembly_courts_and_policy: - **TVK Announces Second Phase of Statewide Educational Awards Ceremony in Chennai:** The ruling Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) has announced that the second phase of its flagship educational awards ceremony will be held on November 18, 2026, at Neelangarai, Chennai. Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay will personally preside over the event to honor students who secured top ranks in the class 10 and 12 public examinations by distributing cash incentives and merit certificates. This initiative builds upon the preliminary awards program held on November 4, which recognized top-performing students across thirty constituencies spanning five districts. Political analysts view these large-scale public felicitation events as a strategic outreach effort by the leadership to consolidate grassroots support among youth and academic communities across Tamil Nadu. ([Polimer News](https://www.polimernews.com/justnownews/tvk-2nd-phase-education-award-ceremony-november-18-12810765))
sections.district_developments: - **Two TVK Functionaries Arrested in Chennai for Alleged Sexual Harassment at Koyambedu Hotel:** City police in Chennai have arrested two local functionaries of the ruling Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) on charges of sexually harassing a 30-year-old female staff member at a star hotel in Koyambedu. The accused individuals, identified as Prabhukumar and Balaji from Arumbakkam, allegedly approached the victim while she was on reception duty in an inebriated state and made explicit sexual advances. Following a formal complaint lodged by hotel management and the victim, law enforcement officers registered a case under relevant sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and effected the arrests. The incident has drawn sharp criticism from opposition parties who point to the episode as evidence of deteriorating public safety and inadequate internal discipline within the ruling party ranks. ([DT Next](https://www.dtnext.in/news/chennai/two-tvk-functionaries-held-for-sexually-harassing-koyambedu-hotel-staffer))
sections.what_to_watch_next: Observers will closely monitor Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay's diplomatic engagements and meetings with Congress national leadership during his New Delhi visit, specifically regarding the contentious Mekedhatu dam project and seat-sharing dynamics. Additionally, upcoming legal proceedings concerning federal ED summons for political figures and the security arrangements for the TVK educational awards ceremony in Chennai on November 18 remain critical focal points over the next 24 to 48 hours.
